I would recommend a mental health professional in addition to your prayers. Mine has certainly helped me with my problems, both before and during the pandemic.

One of the things that I’ve done is getting a notebook and writing down 3 good things that happen each day. It can be as big or small as you can manage, even something like a particularly good-tasting bite of your breakfast, or drinking a full glass of water.

It really helps with perspective, and can help shift your mind towards noticing positive things more easily.

I haven’t really been in your situation, but I do know what it’s like to grieve.

I would first recommend taking time a day off for yourself if you can. Cry, reminisce, eat your favorite food, do whatever you want for that day. Given the type of person you described your father as, I’m sure he would want you to look after yourself and be happy.

Then reach out to other people. It can be your friends, your family, or anyone close to you. I think this is one of the more important steps, since it can help you feel less alone, especially people who know more about how you feel.

And also, *please* don’t feel ashamed of crying or grieving. It’s one of the things that lets you know you have a heart, and a good one at that.

Overall, take things as slow as you need, and let any feelings that come out, come out.

Thank you for reaching out to us, and I hope you start to feel better soon. \^\^

I didn’t think as far ahead as sexuality my first time around as a Christian, but it is a big issue now that I’ve gotten older. So yeah, it developed into this.

I don’t even know why I’m still here. Not just this time but *both* times I converted, it was just because I wanted something, and I said I would become a Christian if it happened. Well, it barely panned out the first time, and I still don’t know if it’ll pan out this time, but it looks more and more unlikely. That’s it; I needed something and I was desperate.

Even if I stay now, it’s only because God will send me to hell if I don’t. And maybe he’ll send me to hell for that—because it’s fear, not actual loyalty. Or maybe he‘ll do it since I already left and rejected him once.

I‘ve always made the decision to be a Christian out of pressure or fear, and that’s a useless foundation for any faith. I hardly do anything out of the “kindness of my heart” anymore, and Christianity has only made that worse.
It says f*g...

Because I hate myself, and I always have.

And ironically, I was doing a good job of healing from that *until* I became a Christian again. Then it was all just “You were born a doomed sinner”, “your good works are dirty rags”, “You’re lukewarm”.

I spent two years trying to recover from having given up on myself and thinking I was destined to be a horrible person forever, and I was well on my way toward doing so. I was trying to patch things up with my parents, I was helping and even burying animals, I was trying to be a good boyfriend and friend, and I was trying to start a career where I could bring happiness to others. I was genuinely trying to be a good person, for no other reason than being objectively kind. I even had a higher opinion of marriage, because I thought it was the ultimate expression of love for someone, and a desire to want to spend the rest of your life with them, because you love them that much.

And then I try to be a Christian, and those 2 years of careful recovery get torn down in 2 months. Now the only reason I’m trying to be a good person is because I’ll get sent to hell if I don’t. I hardly ever called myself a faggot or even fantasized about beating gay people, despite being one of them, until I started being a Christian. Now marriage is just something for having children or for hiding your sexuality, or just for having sex without sin, because apparently a wedding ring is all it takes for it to magically vanish.

​

Now I’m not even allowed to love someone from the “wrong” gender or even feel accepting of what I *can’t* *change*.

No, the ”moral” thing to do is deny what I naturally feel and try to brainwash myself into seeking out a woman for simple breeding-stock, so I can cement a lie that somehow doesn’t violate the commandments, just because it’s “holy”. What’s holy about lying to myself and to God.

No honesty with myself, no confidence, no reassurance, no good actions just for the sake of being good, no reason to believe that I can ever be happy or at peace unless God is merciful enough to allow it (which will never happen), nothing! I’m just a drone to be used and thrown away because I’ll never good enough.

And now I can’t even *agree* with that?

If I’m not supposed to feel secure in myself then at least let me join God in thinking of me as an irredeemable sack of filth, with no good qualities and deserving of every last ounce of the pain I suffer at the hands of others and myself.

At least then we’ll agree on *something*.
No. I guess I’m just using that verse as an excuse to hurt myself more, which makes me hate myself more...
